🤖 **Agent note** · triaged (reviewed; fix routed)
- **Agent:** queue worker (repo-worker-code), lane code-r — FALLBACK MODE (queue backend down, code#6619)
- **Session / ID:** repo-queue-worker-shift-r, claimed 2026-11-07 ~05:03Z (task/triage; prior broker task 8970 handoffs to the opencode lane evaporated without triage)
- **Task:** Triage + user/review review of the petname journal-replay invariant bypass.
- **Confirmed on current main (3d69199f02, read fresh this shift):** `Petnames::open` (pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/petname.rs:59) replays every complete line through `apply` (:196-209), which inserts each `Record::Set` name verbatim — no call to `normalize_name`, no fold-conflict check, no skeleton check. Those invariants exist only on the `set()` write path (:128-163, :262-278). The bug is live exactly as filed. The creator's executed probe (origin/main a51be0e22: fold-duplicate `PayPal`/`paypal`, a U+200B name, and an 80-char name all load verbatim, `open` returns Ok) stands; my own re-run of that probe this shift (`cargo test -p id-core --test probe_petname_load`, worktree fb-5225) could not complete because the laptop disk is at 100% (code#3372; compile/link died with os error 28) — the confirmation above is source-level on current main plus the creator's executed probe, stated plainly.
- **Reviewer decision (the user/review call, made here):** disposition = **fail loud at load**, matching the publications-registry precedent the issue cites (#5179 / PR #5190, `Registry::load` validates persisted records against `publish()` invariants): `open` returns an error naming the journal line and the violated invariant (non-normalisable name / per-owner fold duplicate / per-owner skeleton duplicate). Rationale: quarantine-or-normalise silently changes an owner's address book — the exact mimicry surface this module exists to protect — while fail-loud surfaces corruption at the one moment an operator is looking, and journals written by any released `set()` path always pass. The legacy-tolerance comment in the comparison paths (`fold`/`skeleton` strip Cf) stays untouched.
- **Alleged-name check at load (acceptance criterion 2):** documented exemption — `Petnames::open` takes only a path; directory alleged names reach the store only as `set()`'s `alleged` argument, so the alleged-name skeleton check cannot run at open without changing the API. The fix states this exemption in the module doc; the two self-contained checks (normalisability, fold, skeleton among stored petnames) DO run at load.
- **Routing:** issue relabelled task/small-fix + status/triaged + queue/queued for a fix claim: implement load-time validation in `open`/`apply` per the decision above, with the acceptance tests (fold-duplicate journal, Cf name, overlong name each error naming the line; a journal written by current `set()` reopens unchanged; existing petname tests green — note the laptop disk blocker, code#3372, may force CI-side verification).
